tags.title: Other vendors' models
tags.meaning: It can use models of other makers than its own (here: through a model gateway).

tags.title: Works through OpenRouter
tags.meaning: One OpenRouter key reaches its models.

tags.title: Works through Vercel AI Gateway
tags.meaning: One Vercel AI Gateway key reaches its models.

tags.title: API key
tags.meaning: It works with an API key of its model's provider.

tags.title: Its maker's sign-in
tags.meaning: It can sign in with its maker's own account (a subscription, a ChatGPT plan, an x.ai account).

tags.title: No account needed
tags.meaning: It works with no key and no sign-in.

tags.title: Free tier
tags.meaning: Its model has a free tier (cited, with the date it was checked).

tags.title: Says what it is doing
tags.meaning: It reports its state to Dozer (OSC 7501): working, waiting for you, done.

tags.title: Resumes after a restart
tags.meaning: Its default session continues the last conversation when it is restarted.

tags.title: Runs on Alpine
tags.meaning: It runs on a musl base (Alpine).

tags.title: Open source
tags.meaning: Its source is published under an open-source licence.

tags.title: Runs without a terminal
tags.meaning: It has a non-interactive mode: one prompt in, the answer out (claude -p, codex exec).

kinds.title: Coding agents
kinds.meaning: An agent that works on code in its folder: reads, edits and runs it, in a session you watch.

kinds.title: AI tools
kinds.meaning: Everything else with a model behind it: chat and shell helpers, personal agents, frameworks, evaluation, workflows.

categories.title: Coding agent
categories.meaning: It edits and runs code in its folder, turn by turn (Claude Code, Codex, Aider).

categories.title: Personal agent
categories.meaning: A general assistant that acts for you with shell, file and web tools (OpenClaw, nanobot, gptme).

categories.title: Terminal tool
categories.meaning: A command-line helper: a chat REPL, an answer to a prompt, a shell command from a request (llm, AIChat, ShellGPT).

categories.title: Framework
categories.meaning: A library or kit for building agents and LLM apps, with a command line (smolagents, ADK, CrewAI).

categories.title: Browser agent
categories.meaning: It drives a web browser for you or for another agent (browser-use, Skyvern).

categories.title: MCP
categories.meaning: Model Context Protocol servers, gateways and inspectors.

categories.title: Research
categories.meaning: It searches, reads and reports: deep research, notebooks over your sources.

categories.title: Evaluation
categories.meaning: It tests and red-teams prompts, models and LLM apps (promptfoo, garak).

categories.title: Workflow
categories.meaning: A builder for automations and LLM pipelines, usually with a web UI (n8n, Langflow, Dify).

categories.title: Local models
categories.meaning: It runs models inside the sandbox, with no API key (Ollama, llama.cpp).

categories.title: Chat app
categories.meaning: A chat web app for your models (Open WebUI, LibreChat).
